Counterexample to universal9-node accuracy: axial symmetry is lost near quadrature nodes, despite moment preservation.

model: Normalized receiver-Gaussian spatial average, Gaussian finite emitter with sigma_e=radius/sqrt5; pure CPU volume-only SH1, NOT enabled or GPU tested
limits: No runtime/renderer/shader/source gain/audio changes. CPU tests do not claim appearance accepted.
Positive9 preserves first two density moments but is a Gaussian mixture, NOT the original SPD Gaussian. Large anisotropy/near-source errors are reported, not hidden by passing moment tests.
Isotropic1 preserves normalization, mean and covariance trace only. It does not preserve true cross-section/axial shape.

Emitter is a normalized Gaussian emission volume with sigma_e=R/sqrt5, matching uniform-volume sphere second moment only; not an opaque finite sphere, exact real flame radiance or physical source cap. Point-source Gaussian receiver average is already finite.
No source-to-smoke extinction, cloud/tree occlusion, scattering mass multiplier or view-dependent evaluation. Source T and joint RTE remain absent.
Per-packet field is constant, not conditional-ray-mean varying lighting. SH1 removes l>=2 HG lobes; mean angular flux alone is retained, source/view correlations are not.

Raw SH angular bound is for this constant-field approximation. Add other local/sky terms once; replace pyro slots4/5 rather than adding a duplicate. Never write flash to base sky/environment/GI or apply sceneP inside CPU coefficients.
Node timings are bounded research measurements. Incomplete50ms stress results explicitly stop and cannot be used as a valid partial field or FPS promise.

Finite numerical quadratures and lookup arithmetic are not rigorously outward-rounded global FP16 proofs. Caller must budget maximum C0+norm(C1) over published packets and apply SSA/air/other-source budget consistently.
